resources.string: On-command evaluation and tracking of joint range-of-motion
Project ROM is an application for on-demand measurement of joint range of motion with focus on privacy preservation of the end-user.
Landmarks (or specific body points) are calculated live through artificial intelligence provided by Mediapipe
Resulting before- and after images are saved locally within the context of the application and will be removed on uninstall unless saved as images on your local computer
This application has been developed by Vincent Westlund at the behest of Malmö, and Pittsburgh University.
Every pose has a distinct description and example. Follow these for the best results.
The camera-view offers a simple step-by-step instructions while running.
Align the Green point with the Red circle
Face left or right within the view of the camera. Align the left or right shoulder with the green circle. Relax your arm, start the session and move it in the motion specified in the picture.
Face the camera. Align the left or right shoulder with the green circle. Start the session. Raise your arm up to 45 degrees.

Face left or right within the view of the camera. Align the left or right shoulder with the green circle. Raise your arm to 90 degrees and hold out your forearm as specified. Start the session and move your forearm backwards towards your shoulder.

Face the camera. Align the left or right shoulder with the green circle. Relax your arms and start the session. Move the selected left or right arm backward and the opposite arm forward as specified in the picture.
Face left or right within the view of the camera and align your selected shoulder with the center point. Move your left or right arm in an arc as described by the picture.
Tap Save to confirm. Changes apply the next time you open the camera for an analysis.
